title: Read a chosen file
summary: A file input lets a person choose a file.
introduction: A file input lets a person choose a file. Your task: Try a small text file that you created yourself.
learningObjectives: Try a small text file that you created yourself.
Explain the example for read a chosen file

blocks.text: A file input lets a person choose a file. The page can read that chosen file; it cannot freely browse every file on the computer.

Use these examples in a local page in a current browser. APIs involving files, storage, clipboard or location may need HTTPS, a user action or permission. They are shown as code because this site's sandbox limits those features.

blocks.title: Read a chosen file

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A label's `for` value names the input id. That connection lets the label describe and focus the intended field.
`textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`files[0]` is the first file chosen through this input. It does not grant access to arbitrary files on the computer.

blocks.text: After a text file is chosen, its words appear in the pre element.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use textContent for the file contents. A file may contain text that should never be treated as HTML.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Try a small text file that you created yourself.
